security.otoroshi.io.AdminSession.description: The session of a user logged in to the backoffice. It is created when the user logs in, and removed when it logs out or when it expires: the api reads and deletes them, it does not create nor update them

randomId.description: The id of the session, a random token

name.description: The display name of the user, read from the profile given by the identity provider, or the login (`username`) of an otoroshi admin. Shown in the list of the admin sessions of the backoffice

email.description: The email of the user, or the login of an otoroshi admin: the `allowedUsers` and `deniedUsers` of the module are checked against it, and the `rightsOverride` and `adminEntityValidatorsOverride` of the module are keyed by it

authConfigId.description: The id of the auth module the user logged in with, `none` for an otoroshi admin (login and password or WebAuthn). `none` when missing

profile.description: The profile of the user given by the identity provider. Its shape depends on the provider. `{}` when missing

token.description: The tokens given by the identity provider (access token, refresh token...). Its shape depends on the provider. `{}` when missing

simpleLogin.description: Whether the user is an otoroshi admin that logged in with its login and password, not through an auth module: logging out then only deletes the session, without going through the auth module of the backoffice. False for a WebAuthn login. True when missing

createdAt.description: When the session was created, a timestamp in milliseconds. Now when missing

expiredAt.description: When the session expires, a timestamp in milliseconds. Now when missing

lastRefresh.description: When the tokens of the session were last refreshed, a timestamp in milliseconds. Now when missing

metadata.description: The metadata of the session, free key/value pairs

additionalProperties.description: The value of the metadata

tags.description: Free tags of the session. The built-in login flows leave it empty, a wasm or a workflow auth module sets it in the user it answers

items.description: A tag

rights.description: The rights of the user on the tenants (organizations) and teams of otoroshi. `[{"tenant": "*:rw", "teams": ["*:rw"]}]` makes a super admin

adminEntityValidators.description: The validators the entities written by the user have to pass, by entity kind

additionalProperties.description: The validators of an entity kind, keyed by the singular name of the kind (`route`, `apikey`, `certificate`...) or `all` for every kind. Every validator has to pass for the entity to be written

route.error: routes can only be exposed on oto.tools

security.otoroshi.io.AuthModule.description: An auth module: how the users log in to the private apps (the routes using the `Authentication` plugin) or to the backoffice. Its `type` selects the identity provider: in memory users (`basic`), OAuth2 / OpenID Connect (`oauth2`), LDAP (`ldap`), SAML v2 (`saml`), OAuth 1.0a (`oauth1`), or a login flow implemented by a wasm plugin (`wasm`) or a workflow (`workflow`). The template of a type is served by `_template?type=<type>`

example.name: Keycloak
example.desc: Login with the Keycloak of the company

BasicAuthModuleConfig.description: An in memory auth module: its users and their passwords are stored in the module itself

type.description: The type of the auth module, `basic` for an in memory auth module

id.description: The unique id of the auth module, named by the `module` of the `Authentication` plugin of the routes, the `modules` of the `Multi Authentication` plugin, or the `backOfficeAuthRef` of the global configuration

basicAuth.description: Also accept the credentials of an `Authorization: Basic` header, without going through the login page. False when missing

sessionMaxAge.description: How long a session lasts, in seconds. 86400 (a day) when missing

metadata.description: The metadata of the auth module, free key/value pairs

additionalProperties.description: The value of the metadata

clientId.description: The client id of otoroshi on the identity provider. `client` when missing

clientSecret.description: The client secret of otoroshi on the identity provider. It can be a vault reference like `${vault://local/client-secret}`. `secret` when missing

authorizeUrl.description: The authorization endpoint of the identity provider

tokenUrl.description: The token endpoint of the identity provider, called to exchange the authorization code for the tokens

userInfoUrl.description: The userinfo endpoint of the identity provider, called to get the profile of the user

introspectionUrl.description: The token introspection endpoint (RFC 7662) of the identity provider, used to check opaque access tokens

loginUrl.description: The url the users are redirected to in order to log in, usually the authorization endpoint

logoutUrl.description: The url the users are redirected to when they log out, the client id being added to it. Nothing is called when empty

scope.description: The scopes asked to the identity provider, separated by spaces. `openid profile email name` when missing

claims.description: The `claims` parameter sent to the identity provider, not sent when empty. `email name` when missing

useCookie.description: Keep the route the user comes from in a cookie instead of a query parameter of the redirect uri, for the identity providers that refuse query parameters in redirect uris. False when missing

useJson.description: Send the payloads of the calls to the token, userinfo and introspection endpoints as json instead of form urlencoded. False when missing

pkce.description: The PKCE settings of the authorization code flow, null to not use PKCE

noWildcardRedirectURI.description: Send the callback url as is as the redirect uri, without query parameters, as OAuth 2.1 requires. False when missing

readProfileFromToken.description: Read the profile of the user from the claims of the access token, verified with `jwtVerifier`, instead of calling the userinfo endpoint. Only used when `jwtVerifier` is set. False when missing

accessTokenField.description: The field of the answer of the token endpoint holding the access token. `access_token` when missing

jwtVerifier.description: How the signature of the access tokens of the identity provider is verified when the profile of the user is read from them (`readProfileFromToken`), null when the profile comes from the userinfo endpoint

nameField.description: The field of the profile holding the name of the user. `name` when missing

emailField.description: The field of the profile holding the email of the user. `email` when missing

apiKeyMetaField.description: The field of the profile holding the metadata of the api keys the user creates (client credentials). `apkMeta` when missing

apiKeyTagsField.description: The field of the profile holding the tags of the api keys the user creates (client credentials). `apkTags` when missing

otoroshiDataField.description: The path of the field of the profile holding the otoroshi data of the user (sent to the backends), the parts of the path being separated by `|`. `app_metadata | otoroshi_data` when missing

callbackUrl.description: The url the identity provider redirects the users to once logged in: the callback of the private apps, or the one of the backoffice (`/backoffice/auth0/callback`)

oidConfig.description: The url of the OpenID Connect discovery document of the identity provider (ending with `.well-known/openid-configuration`), null when the endpoints are set by hand

mtlsConfig.description: The tls settings of the calls to the identity provider

proxy.description: The http proxy of the calls to the identity provider, null to use the auth proxy of the global configuration

extraMetadata.description: A json object merged into the otoroshi data of the users that log in, sent to the backends of the private apps

metadata.description: The metadata of the auth module, free key/value pairs. They are copied to the sessions of the users that log in to the private apps

additionalProperties.description: The value of the metadata

tags.description: Free tags of the auth module, to search and sort it. They are copied to the sessions of the users that log in to the private apps

items.description: A tag

refreshTokens.description: Refresh the access token of the users with their refresh token when it expires. False when missing

sessionCookieValues.description: The `HttpOnly` and `Secure` flags of the session cookies set on the private apps once a user has logged in through the module. Both true when missing

superAdmins.description: Give super admin rights to every user that logs in to the backoffice. When false, the rights come from `rightsOverride`, then from the `otoroshiRightsField` of the profile, then from the location of the module. JsonPathValidator.description: A check of a json document: the value found at a json path of the document is compared to an expected value. It checks the profile of a logged in user (user validators of auth modules) or the json of an entity an admin writes (admin entity validators)

value.description: The expected value: any json value, compared as is to the value found at the path. A string can hold an operator instead: `IsDefined()` and `NotDefined()` check the presence of the path, `Not(x)`, `Regex(x)`, `RegexNot(x)`, `Wildcard(x)`, `WildcardNot(x)`, `Contains(x)`, `ContainsNot(x)`, `StartsWith(x)`, `DontStartsWith(x)`, `ContainedIn(a, b)`, `NotContainedIn(a, b)`, `JsonContains(x)` and `JsonContainsNot(x)` check a string, `Size(n)`, `SizeNot(n)`, `SizeGt(n)`, `SizeGte(n)`, `SizeLt(n)`, `SizeLte(n)`, `Contains(x)`, `Contains(Regex(x))` and `Contains(Wildcard(x))` check an array

type.description: The kind of verifier, always `global` for the verifiers of the admin api. Not read, always written

source.description: Where the token is found in the requests

algoSettings.description: How the signature of the token is verified. For the `DefaultToken` strategy, how the generated token is signed

strategy.description: What the verifier does with the token

metadata.description: The metadata of the verifier, free key/value pairs

additionalProperties.description: The value of the metadata

tags.description: Free tags of the jwt verifier, to search and sort it

JwtTokenLocation.description: Where a jwt token is in a request: a header (`InHeader`), a query parameter (`InQueryParam`) or a cookie (`InCookie`)

InQueryParam.description: A jwt token read from a query parameter of the request

type.description: The location of the token, always `InQueryParam`

name.description: The name of the query parameter holding the token

InHeader.description: A jwt token read from a header of the request. When otoroshi writes a token (signed or transformed), it is written in the same header, prefixed by `remove`

type.description: The location of the token, always `InHeader`

name.description: The name of the header holding the token

remove.description: A text removed from the value of the header to get the token, like `Bearer ` (with its trailing space). Empty when missing

InCookie.description: A jwt token read from a cookie of the request

type.description: The location of the token, always `InCookie`

name.description: The name of the cookie holding the token

AlgoSettings.description: How the signature of a jwt token is verified, or how a token is signed. Its `type` selects the algorithm and where the keys come from: a shared secret (`HSAlgoSettings`), PEM keys (`RSAlgoSettings`, `ESAlgoSettings`), a key pair of a certificate of otoroshi (`RSAKPAlgoSettings`, `ESKPAlgoSettings`), the key pair matching the `kid` of the token (`KidAlgoSettings`) or a remote JSON Web Key Set (`JWKSAlgoSettings`)

HSAlgoSettings.description: Tokens signed with HMAC and SHA-2 (`HS256`, `HS384`, `HS512`) using a shared secret

type.description: The algorithm settings, always `HSAlgoSettings`

size.description: The size of the SHA-2 hash of the algorithm, in bits: 256, 384 or 512 (`HS256`, `HS384`, `HS512`)

secret.description: The shared secret. It can be a vault reference like `${vault://local/jwt-secret}`, or an expression like `${env.JWT_SECRET}` or `${config.jwt.secret}`

base64.description: The secret is base64 encoded, it is decoded before use. False when missing

RSAlgoSettings.description: Tokens signed with RSA and SHA-2 (`RS256`, `RS384`, `RS512`) using the keys given in PEM format

type.description: The algorithm settings, always `RSAlgoSettings`

size.description: The size of the SHA-2 hash of the algorithm, in bits: 256, 384 or 512 (`RS256`, `RS384`, `RS512` for instance)

publicKey.description: The RSA public key in PEM format, used to verify the tokens. It can be a vault reference like `${vault://local/jwt-public-key}`, or an expression like `${env.JWT_PUBLIC_KEY}`

privateKey.description: The RSA private key in PEM format, only needed to sign tokens (re-signing strategies, default token), null otherwise

ESAlgoSettings.description: Tokens signed with ECDSA and SHA-2 (`ES256`, `ES384`, `ES512`) using the keys given in PEM format

type.description: The algorithm settings, always `ESAlgoSettings`

size.description: The size of the SHA-2 hash of the algorithm, in bits: 256, 384 or 512 (`ES256`, `ES384`, `ES512`)

publicKey.description: The EC public key in PEM format, used to verify the tokens. It can be a vault reference like `${vault://local/jwt-public-key}`, or an expression like `${env.JWT_PUBLIC_KEY}`

privateKey.description: The EC private key in PEM format, only needed to sign tokens (re-signing strategies, default token), null otherwise

JWKSAlgoSettings.description: Tokens verified with the public keys of a remote JSON Web Key Set, like the `jwks_uri` of an OpenID Connect provider. The key is chosen by the `kid` of the token. The key set is cached for `ttl` milliseconds. Only verifies tokens, it cannot sign them

type.description: The algorithm settings, always `JWKSAlgoSettings`

url.description: The url of the JSON Web Key Set

timeout.description: The timeout of the call fetching the key set, in milliseconds. 2000 when missing

headers.description: The http headers sent with the call fetching the key set

additionalProperties.description: The value of the header

ttl.description: How long the fetched key set is cached, in milliseconds. 3600000 (one hour) when missing

kty.description: The type of the keys of the key set (`RSA` or `EC` to verify RSA or ECDSA signatures). `RSA` when missing

proxy.description: The http proxy used to fetch the key set, null to use the jwk proxy of the global configuration

tls_config.description: A copy of `mtlsConfig`, written for the older clients. It is only read when `mtlsConfig` and `tlsConfig` are missing

mtlsConfig.description: The tls settings of the call fetching the key set. The legacy `tlsConfig` and `tls_config` keys are read when it is missing

RSAKPAlgoSettings.description: Tokens signed with RSA and SHA-2 (`RS256`, `RS384`, `RS512`) using the key pair of a certificate of otoroshi

type.description: The algorithm settings, always `RSAKPAlgoSettings`

size.description: The size of the SHA-2 hash of the algorithm, in bits: 256, 384 or 512 (`RS256`, `RS384`, `RS512` for instance)

certId.description: The id of the certificate holding the RSA key pair. Its id is also the `kid` of the tokens otoroshi signs

ESKPAlgoSettings.description: Tokens signed with ECDSA and SHA-2 (`ES256`, `ES384`, `ES512`) using the key pair of a certificate of otoroshi

type.description: The algorithm settings, always `ESKPAlgoSettings`

size.description: The size of the SHA-2 hash of the algorithm, in bits: 256, 384 or 512 (`ES256`, `ES384`, `ES512`)

certId.description: The id of the certificate holding the EC key pair. Its id is also the `kid` of the tokens otoroshi signs

KidAlgoSettings.description: Tokens verified with the key pair of the certificate of otoroshi whose id is the `kid` of the token. Only verifies tokens, it cannot sign them

type.description: The algorithm settings, always `KidAlgoSettings`

onlyExposedCerts.description: Only use the key pairs of the certificates that are `exposed`, whose public keys otoroshi serves in its jwks (`/.well-known/otoroshi/security/jwks.json`). When false, any key pair of otoroshi can verify a token. False when missing

VerifierStrategy.description: What a jwt verifier does with the token of a request. Its `type` selects it: verify the token and send it unchanged (`PassThrough`), verify it and sign it again (`Sign`), verify it, rewrite it and sign it again (`Transform`), or generate a token when the request has none (`DefaultToken`)

DefaultToken.description: Generates a token when the request has none. In strict mode the token is signed with the `algoSettings` of the verifier and written in its `source`, and a request already holding a token is refused. Otherwise a request without token goes through without one, and a request holding one has it verified

type.description: The strategy, always `DefaultToken`

strict.description: Generate the token for the requests without one, and refuse the requests that already hold one. True when missing

token.description: The claims of the generated token. The string values can hold expressions like `${apikey.clientName}`, `${token.jti}`, `${token.iat}`, `${token.nbf}`, `${token.exp}` (in a minute), `${token.iss}` (`Otoroshi`), `${token.sub}` (the `clientName` of the api key, or the email of the user, `anonymous` otherwise) and `${token.aud}` (`backend`) giving default values. The `iat`, `nbf` and `exp` claims are converted to numbers

verificationSettings.description: The claims a token found in the request has to hold

PassThrough.description: Verifies the token of the request (signature and claims) and sends it unchanged to the backend

type.description: The strategy, always `PassThrough`

verificationSettings.description: The claims the token has to hold

Sign.description: Verifies the token of the request with the `algoSettings` of the verifier, then signs it again with other algorithm settings before sending it to the backend

type.description: The strategy, always `Sign`

verificationSettings.description: The claims the token has to hold

algoSettings.description: How the token sent to the backend is signed

Transform.description: Verifies the token of the request with the `algoSettings` of the verifier, rewrites its claims, then signs it again with other algorithm settings and sends it to the backend at another location

type.description: The strategy, always `Transform`

verificationSettings.description: The claims the token has to hold

transformSettings.description: How the token is rewritten, and where it is sent

algoSettings.description: How the token sent to the backend is signed

VerificationSettings.description: The claims a jwt token has to hold, on top of a valid signature

fields.description: The expected values of the claims of the token, keyed by claim name. `iss`, `aud`, `sub` and `jti` are compared to their value, other claims accept the operators `Regex(x)`, `RegexNot(x)`, `Wildcard(x)`, `WildcardNot(x)`, `Contains(x)`, `ContainsNot(x)`, `ContainsOneOf(a, b)`, `ContainsNotOneOf(a, b)`, `ContainsAll(a, b)`... The values can hold expressions like `${req.headers.X-Tenant}`

additionalProperties.description: The expected value of the claim

arrayFields.description: The values an array claim of the token has to contain, keyed by claim name. Several values are separated by commas, the claim has to contain all of them

additionalProperties.description: The value, or the comma separated values, the array claim has to contain

TransformSettings.description: Where the transformed jwt token is sent to the backend, and how its claims are rewritten

location.description: Where the transformed token is written in the request sent to the backend

mappingSettings.description: How the claims of the token are rewritten

MappingSettings.description: How the claims of a jwt token are rewritten before the token is signed again

map.description: The claims to rename: the name of a claim of the token, mapped to its new name

additionalProperties.description: The new name of the claim

values.description: The claims added to the token, by name. The string values can hold expressions like `${apikey.clientName}` or `${token.sub}`

remove.description: The names of the claims removed from the token

items.description: The name of a claim
